title: Arizona Contractor Lead Database Research
summary: Research on databases for pre-qualified AZ contractor leads without Apollo credits.
content:
Niche Database Research: Arizona Contractor Lead Sources

Jacob, 2026-03-12. Research on databases that give us pre-qualified contractor leads without spending Apollo credits.

1. Arizona Registrar of Contractors (AZ ROC)

URL: https://roc.az.gov Verdict: THE GOLD MINE. Use this first.

What's Available

  • Online search tool: https://azroc.my.site.com/AZRoc/s/contractor-search

    • Search by license type (Commercial, Residential, Dual)
    • Filter by city name
    • Filter by license classification (HVAC = C-39, Plumbing = C-37, Electrical = C-11, General Commercial = B-1, General Residential = B)
    • Shows: license number, business name, license status, classification, qualifying party name
    • FREE. No login required.

  • Posting list / CSV downloads: https://roc.az.gov/posting-list

    • ROC publishes downloadable lists of all active licenses
    • Previous research found CSV files at URLs like: roc.az.gov/sites/default/files/ROC_Posting-List_Commercial_YYYY-MM-DD.csv
    • Data fields in CSV: License number, business name, license classification, address, city, state, zip, qualifying party name, issued date, expiration date, status
    • Note: Could not confirm the posting list page is still active with current CSV links. The online search tool is confirmed working.

How Jacob Uses This

  1. Use the online search tool to pull contractors by classification + city (Phoenix, Scottsdale, Mesa, Tempe, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Peoria)
  2. Focus on: C-39 (HVAC), C-37 (Plumbing), C-11 (Electrical), B-1 (General Commercial), B (General Residential)
  3. Every result is a state-licensed, active contractor. Pre-qualified by definition.
  4. Use Apollo ONLY for enrichment: plug in company name/domain to find owner's personal email. Stop using info@ addresses.

Why It Matters

45,000+ active licenses in Arizona. This is the complete list. No guessing, no hoping Apollo surfaces the right companies. Filter by Phoenix metro zip codes and AOM's target classifications, and we have hundreds of leads for free.

2. MTCAZ (Mechanical Trade Contractors of Arizona)

URL: https://mtcaz.org Verdict: High-value but gated. Partnership is the play.

What's Available

  • Trade association for HVAC, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration contractors in Arizona
  • 310 member companies (per previous research)
  • Contact: 1904 W. Mountain View Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85021 / (602) 298-5454
  • Member directory appears to be behind a login/members-only section
  • They run education/training events in Phoenix, Tucson, and Yuma

How to Access

  • Option A (best): Patrik already sent a partnership email to MTCAZ pitching a member spotlight video series. If that partnership moves forward, AOM would naturally get access to the full member list.
  • Option B: Attend MTCAZ events and collect contacts in person.
  • Option C: Request the directory directly. Call (602) 298-5454 and ask if the member list is available publicly or if AOM can access it as a potential service provider.

Why It Matters

These are the most established HVAC/mechanical contractors in Arizona. They pay membership dues, which means they invest in their business. They're organized, professional, and more likely to value marketing. Ideal AOM prospects.

3. BBB Phoenix (Better Business Bureau)

URL: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix Verdict: Free, browsable, good for filtering quality companies.

What's Available

Public directory of BBB-rated businesses, searchable by category and location. No login required.

Direct category links for AOM's targets:

  • Air Conditioning Contractors: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/air-conditioning-contractor
  • Plumbing and Heating: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/plumbing-and-heating
  • Plumber: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/plumber
  • General Contractor: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/general-contractor
  • Commercial Contractors: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/commercial-contractors
  • Building Contractors: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/building-contractors
  • Electrical Contractors: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/electrical-contractors
  • Excavating Contractors: https://www.bbb.org/us/az/phoenix/category/excavating-contractors

Data per listing: Business name, address, phone, BBB rating (A+ to F), accreditation status, years in business, customer reviews.

How Jacob Uses This

  1. Browse each category above. Collect company names and domains.
  2. Prioritize BBB-accredited (A/A+ rated) contractors. They already care about their public image, which means they're more likely to invest in marketing.
  3. Cross-reference with ROC data for license verification.
  4. Use Apollo for owner email enrichment on the best prospects.

Why It Matters

BBB accreditation is a quality signal. These companies pay for their BBB membership and maintain their rating. They're established, care about reputation, and have marketing budgets. Perfect AOM targets.

4. Google Business Profiles (Phoenix HVAC/Plumbing/Electrical)

Verdict: Useful for research and personalization. Not great for bulk lead generation.

What's Available

  • Search Google Maps for "Phoenix HVAC contractor" (or plumbing, electrical, general contractor)
  • Results show: business name, address, phone, website, Google rating, review count, photos, hours
  • ByteScraper lists 274 HVAC contractors in Phoenix alone: https://bytescraper.com/b2b-database/state/United-States/Arizona/list-of-hvac-contractors-in-phoenix
  • DownToBid lists 15 best commercial HVAC contractors in Phoenix: https://downtobid.com/contractors/hvac/phoenix

How Jacob Uses This

  1. NOT for bulk lead generation. Google doesn't export results easily.
  2. YES for personalization. Once we have a company name from ROC or BBB, check their Google profile for: star rating, review count, recent photos, owner responses to reviews. This gives Jacob real personalization material for emails.
  3. 4+ star filter is a quality signal. Companies with high ratings and lots of reviews are active, care about their reputation, and are more likely to respond to a professional outreach.

Limitation

No easy way to export Google Business listings in bulk. Manual process. Best used as a research supplement to the other databases, not a primary lead source.

5. Bonus Databases Found During Research

Arizona Builders Alliance (ABA)

  • URL: https://azbuilders.org
  • 380+ member companies in commercial/industrial construction
  • 2025 Membership Directory published online: https://digital.bnpmedia.com/article/2025+ABA+Membership+Directory/4938227/841994/article.html
  • These are bigger outfits with marketing budgets. Premium targets for $3k/month retainers.
  • Phoenix and Tucson offices. Phone: 602-274-8222.

Arizona Mechanical Contractors Association (AMCA)

  • URL: https://arizonamca.org
  • Separate from MTCAZ. Has a public contractor members page: https://arizonamca.org/contractor-members/
  • Also has an affiliates directory: https://arizonamca.org/membership/affiliates-directory/
  • Member search available at: https://arizonamca.org/member-search-results/
  • Known members: University Mechanical (Tempe), Summa Mechanical Contractors (Phoenix), Trident Mechanical (Phoenix), WD Manor.

Other Directories

Source URL Notes
ASA of Arizona https://www.asa-az.org/ Subcontractor members. Est. 1984.
AZAGC https://www.azagc.org/ General contractors since 1934. Member directory available.
Arizona Building Trades https://azbuildingtrades.org/our-members/ Union trade contractors. Member list on site.
Arizona Construction Trades (ACT) https://actaz.net/ Free contractor referral system. Browsable.
Arizona Builders' Zone https://builderszone.com/directory/trade-associations/ Directory of all AZ trade associations.
AZNECA https://azneca.org/ National Electrical Contractors Association, AZ chapter.

Recommended Lead Build Process (Ranked by ROI)

  1. AZ ROC online search (free, immediate). Filter Phoenix metro by HVAC, plumbing, electrical, general. This is the most complete source.
  2. BBB category browse (free, immediate). Focus on A/A+ rated. Cross-reference with ROC.
  3. AMCA contractor members page (free, immediate). Public list of mechanical contractors.
  4. ABA 2025 Membership Directory (free, browsable online). 380 commercial contractors.
  5. MTCAZ directory (gated). Pursue through partnership conversation already in progress.
  6. Apollo enrichment (costs credits). ONLY for finding owner emails after we have company names from the above sources. Confirm with Patrik before any enrichment spend.
  7. Google Business profiles (free). Use for personalization research on specific prospects, not bulk discovery.

This process gives Jacob hundreds of pre-qualified, Phoenix-area construction leads without spending a dollar on Apollo discovery credits. The databases do the discovery. Apollo only does the enrichment.

Scraping Results (Mar 12, 2026)

What Was Successfully Scraped

AMCA (arizonamca.org/contractor-members/): FULL SUCCESS. 22 contractor members extracted including company names, contact person names, phone numbers, addresses, and websites. All data saved to projects/jacob/az-roc-leads.md Tier 1 section. Key Phoenix-area contacts: EMCOR Services Mesa Energy, Harder Mechanical, Southland Industries, Hayes Mechanical, Hudson Services, Coleman Plumbing & Heating, Kinetics, plus 12 more.

BBB Phoenix (bbb.org): PARTIAL SUCCESS. Extracted top 15 listings per category from embedded page JSON:

  • Air Conditioning Contractors: 2,720 total results in BBB system. 15 extracted (page 1).
  • Plumber: 15 extracted.
  • Electrical Contractors: 15 extracted.
  • General Contractor: 15 extracted.
  • Commercial Contractors: 15 extracted.
  • Building Contractors: 15 extracted. All A+ or A rated. Phone numbers included. No owner names (BBB doesn't show those).

What Was Blocked

AZ ROC (roc.az.gov): BLOCKED by Cloudflare JavaScript challenge on both the posting list page and the Salesforce search portal. curl/programmatic access returns a "Just a moment..." challenge page. Requires a real browser session. The ROC posting list CSV (the 45,000+ record goldmine) needs manual download in a browser.

ABA (azbuilders.org): Member directory page served a form/gated content. Could not extract member listings programmatically. The digital.bnpmedia.com 2025 directory also needs a browser to navigate the digital publication viewer.

Recommendations for Patrik/Mac

To unlock the full lead database:

  1. Open roc.az.gov/posting-list in Safari/Chrome. Look for CSV download links for Commercial and Residential posting lists. Save to projects/jacob/.
  2. Open azroc.my.site.com/AZRoc/s/contractor-search. Search C-39 (HVAC) + Phoenix. Export or screenshot results. Repeat for C-37, C-11, B-1, B.
  3. Open digital.bnpmedia.com ABA directory. Screenshot or copy the 380+ member listings.
  4. Run Playwright (via Elmo) on BBB category pages to scrape pages 2+ of each category. Thousands more listings available.

Total Leads Collected This Session

  • AMCA: 19 unique Phoenix-metro contractors (3 already known)
  • BBB: ~75 unique listings across 6 categories (some duplicates across categories)
  • Net new unique prospects: ~80+
  • Top 50 ranked and ready for outreach in projects/jacob/az-roc-leads.md
